Refer to the sketches on the mid-latitude cyclone. What is the name of the boundary between two air masses, as shown in sketch A?
Give ONE reason why the boundary between the two air masses in sketch A would form a wave.
subQuestions.memoText: Atmospheric instability (1) / Frictional drag (1) / Jet streams (1) / Orographic features (accept examples) (1) / Temperature differences (1) / Windspeed differences (1). [ANY ONE] (1 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the stage of development of the mid-latitude cyclone associated with weather conditions in photographs C and D.
Explain how the weather conditions illustrated in photographs C and D developed during the stage named in QUESTION 1.3.3.
subQuestions.memoText: Steep pressure gradient results in gale force/strong winds (2); Strong updraughts/rapid upliftment results in (cumulonimbus clouds) heavy rainfall (2); Air behind the cold front undercuts the warm air ahead of it gives rise to (cumulonimbus clouds) and heavy rainfall (2). [ANY TWO - MUST MENTION GALE FORCE/STRONG WINDS AND HEAVY RAINFALL] (2 x 2). Part marking (any one, maximum one mark): Steep pressure gradient (1); Strong updraughts/rapid upliftment (1); Air behind the cold front undercuts the warm air (1).

subQuestions.questionText:
In the ANSWER BOOK, draw a fully labelled cross-section of a cold front (E–F) in sketch B. Clearly indicate the following:
(a) Correct cross-section
(b) General direction of movement of the mid-latitude cyclone
(c) Cloud type
(d) Sector
subQuestions.memoText: Marks will be allocated for: Correct cross-section drawing (1); Direction of movement of system (1); One type of cloud (Cb/Cu) (1); One sector (1). (4 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to sketch B. Explain how the difference in temperature of the air masses behind the cold front and ahead of the warm front will result in the formation of a cold front occlusion.
subQuestions.memoText: The air behind the cold front is colder than the air in front of the warm front (2); The cold air behind the cold front undercuts the warmer air in front of the warm front (2); The warmer (less dense) air is uplifted over the colder (denser) air (2). (2 x 2). Part marking (maximum two marks): The air behind the cold front is colder (1); The cold air behind the cold front undercuts (1); The warmer (less dense) air is uplifted (1).

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the infographic on Tropical Cyclone Dikeledi. According to the fact file, in which stage of development was Tropical Cyclone Dikeledi on 8 January 2025?
Give TWO reasons in the fact file to support your answer to QUESTION 1.4.1.
subQuestions.memoText: The pressure in the centre is 996 hPa (1); Wind speed is 75 km/h (1); (Accept: it has been given a name) (1). [ANY TWO] (2 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to location map B. Explain why Tropical Cyclone Dikeledi developed between 5° and 20° south of the equator.
subQuestions.memoText: Coriolis force is present within these latitudes resulting in deflection (2); High temperatures/warm oceans promote high evaporation rate (2); Latent heat released during condensation (2); High evaporation rate will lead to intense low pressure (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2). Part marking (maximum two marks): Coriolis force is present (1); High temperatures/warm oceans (1); Latent heat (1); High evaporation rate (1).

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the satellite images C and D. Describe the weather conditions associated with the forward left-hand quadrant (dangerous semicircle) in satellite image D.
subQuestions.memoText: Hurricane force/strength/very strong destructive winds (2); Torrential rainfall/heavy rainfall/thunderstorms (2); Hailstorms (2); Lightning (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why Tropical Cyclone Dikeledi intensified from 8 January to 13 January 2025.
subQuestions.memoText: It moved from land/Madagascar to the warmer waters (Mozambique channel) resulting in increased evaporation/latent heat (2); Less frictional drag over the ocean increases the wind speed (2); (Central) pressure dropped (996 hPa to 976 hPa) due to warmer ocean (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2). Part marking (maximum two marks): It moved from land/Madagascar to the warmer waters (1); Less frictional drag over the ocean (1); (Central) pressure dropped (996 hPa to 976 hPa) (1).

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the synoptic weather map showing South African berg winds. Name ONE South African city indicated on the synoptic weather map that is experiencing berg wind conditions.
Give evidence from the synoptic weather map to support your answer to QUESTION 1.5.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Large temperature range (2); High air temperatures/Air temperature of 34°C/27°C (2); Low humidity/dry air/clear sky (2); (Accept: presence of Kalahari HP and coastal LP) (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the processes that lead to berg winds being warm and dry.
subQuestions.memoText: TEMPERATURE: The air descends (from the interior) down the escarpment (2); The air is heated adiabatically (1°C/100 m) (2). [ANY ONE]. MOISTURE: Moisture is evaporated as air descends (from the interior to the coast) (2). [MUST INCLUDE TEMPERATURE AND MOISTURE] (2 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: The warm and dry conditions can influence veld fires. In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, suggest sustainable strategies that can be put in place to reduce the negative impact of veld fires.
subQuestions.memoText: Create firebreaks/buffer zone (2); Build water storage facilities (2); Educate community about strategies they could implement (2); Make emergency services accessible (2); Access to fire-fighting equipment (2); Implement early warning systems (2); Create emergency assembly points (2); Create awareness (2); Create lookout towers (2); Install sprinklers (2); Evacuation routes and plans (2); Remove alien vegetation/plants (which is flammable) (2). [ANY FOUR - accept examples] (4 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Classify EACH of the temporary base levels in sketch A as either natural or human-made.

subQuestions.memoText: It is the lowest (ultimate) level to which a river can erode (2). [CONCEPT] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to cross-profiles C and D. Differentiate between the shapes of the cross-profiles at C and D.
subQuestions.memoText: Profile C is a closed V-shaped (narrow, deep and steep sided) whereas profile D is an open U-shaped (very wide and gently sloping) (2). [MUST MENTION BOTH PROFILES] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the main processes that give rise to the difference in the shape of cross-profiles C and D.
subQuestions.memoText: Profile C: Vertical/downward erosion is dominant in the upper course (2). Profile D: Deposition is dominant in the lower course (2) / Lateral erosion occurs (2) [ANY ONE]. [MUST REFER TO BOTH PROFILE C AND D] (2 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to photographs A and B showing meanders. Meanders are more likely to form in the (upper/lower) stage/course of a river.
Account for the gentle gradient of the inner bank at C in photograph A.
subQuestions.memoText: Due to deposition (2) / Slow movement/velocity of water (2). [ANY ONE] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to photograph B and cross-section E–F. How does the process of river rejuvenation lead to the formation of incised meanders?
subQuestions.memoText: River rejuvenation results in vertical (downward) erosion (2); Results in a deeper stream channel/valley (due to vertical erosion) (2). (2 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to photograph A. In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, explain how an oxbow lake is formed.
subQuestions.memoText: Continuous (lateral) erosion takes place on the outer bank/under-cut slope (2); Deposition on the inner bank/slip-off slope (2); Meander neck narrows (2); River floods and cuts through meander neck (2); Meander loop is separated from the main stream (by deposition resulting in an ox-bow lake) (2). [ANY FOUR] (4 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the extract and photograph on catchment and river management. According to the extract, why are dense settlements along rivers associated with pollution?
subQuestions.memoText: Poor service provision (1); Do not have means to pay for waste removal services (1); Piled up waste in the settlement is disposed of in the river (1). [ANY ONE] (1 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons from the photograph to support your answer to QUESTION 2.5.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Evidence of solid waste (accept examples) (1); No infrastructure to remove waste (accept examples) (1); No evidence of potable water (1). [ANY TWO] (2 x 1)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the rise in the water level of the river will negatively affect the houses (in the photograph) due to their location.
subQuestions.memoText: Houses are close to the river and could easily flood (2); River banks could collapse destroying houses (accept examples) (2). [ANY ONE - MAXIMUM ONE MARK] (1 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the negative impact of poor river management on the health of rivers.
subQuestions.memoText: Reduced water quality (accept examples) (2); Damages habitat for aquatic life (2); Destroys aquatic life (accept examples) (2); Destroys food chains/food webs (2); Causes eutrophication (accept examples) (2); Disrupt ecosystems (2); Loss of biodiversity (2); Increased sedimentation (accept examples) (2). [ANY TWO] (2 x 2)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest strategies that the municipality can put in place to ensure the sustainability of the river in the photograph.
subQuestions.memoText: Relocate the people (2); Create a buffer zone (2); Create awareness campaigns (accept examples) (2); Educate people on river management (accept examples) (2); Encourage people not to build houses on the river bank (2); Implement legislation (2); Impose fines (2); Plant more vegetation (accept examples) (2); Provide more refuse removal facilities (accept examples) (2); Continuous monitoring/testing (2); Encourage community involvement (accept examples) (2); Provide incentives to people (accept examples) (2); Encourage the recycling of waste (2); Build proper sanitation/drainage systems/water treatment plants (2); Maintain infrastructure (2). [ANY THREE] (3 x 2)
